items.stem: An EPC contractor transfers control of its work to the customer continuously as construction proceeds. How is revenue recognised?

options.text: Over time, using a measure of progress toward completion
options.rationale: Correct: when control transfers over time, revenue is recognised over time by progress.

options.text: Only at the final handover of the asset
options.rationale: Point-in-time recognition does not apply when over-time criteria are met.

options.text: When each invoice is paid in cash
options.rationale: Revenue follows performance, not cash receipt.

options.text: Equally in each calendar month regardless of progress
options.rationale: Recognition follows measured progress, not a flat monthly split.

items.explanation: Correct: when control transfers over time, revenue is recognised over time using a progress measure.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO figures are needed to forecast an EPC contract's final outcome under a cost-based progress method? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: costs to date are part of measuring progress and forecasting.
Correct: cost-to-complete is required to forecast total cost and margin.
A bonus target is irrelevant to the contract forecast.
Marketing spend does not enter the contract forecast.

items.explanation: Correct: costs incurred to date plus estimated cost-to-complete drive the cost-based forecast.

items.stem: Revenue from an unapproved, disputed claim should generally be:

options.text: Constrained and recognised only to the extent it is highly probable it will not reverse
options.rationale: Correct: variable consideration from claims is constrained until highly probable.

options.text: Recognised in full immediately as billed
options.rationale: Disputed claim revenue is uncertain and must be constrained.
Once approved it is recognised; it is not ignored permanently.
Claim revenue is not a fixed asset.

items.explanation: Correct: claim revenue is variable consideration, recognised only to the extent it is highly probable not to reverse.
